findings: A second agent session on the same machine, sharing this working tree and the VPS, developed the same tooling concurrently and rewrote tools mid-run (three tools at 21:02:19Z, 19 s before an evidence run). Sixteen-plus P11 runs between 17:00 and 20:50Z are not attributable to this stream and disagree with it on NC results. The byte set was therefore frozen and every required run re-executed afterwards. Failure record 20261019T2135Z.

NC1 in the first frozen-byte NC run was invalidated by a foreign sik_p6f fixture re-created 46 s after a teardown; the NC driver reuses an existing fixture. A clean re-run discriminates. The driver's fixture-reuse behaviour was a latent defect in that candidate; it is fixed in the re-pinned bytes (0bba1931..., ensure_fx), see the later finding.

An ad-hoc live-proof hash computed by this stream used a tab join and printed 356355:424624d9...; the canonical pipe-join recipe gives 356355:a66a3a54... on the same data. No live change; the wrong value was discarded, not reported as a state change.
Earlier P11 evidence (NC 5/5 at 13:56Z, suite 39/39 at 15:10Z, preservation PASS at 15:32Z) was produced by tool bytes that no longer exist; it is retained in evidence/p11/ but not relied on.

The NC driver's fixture reuse (the latent defect named in the previous revision) was fixed by ensure_fx: before each arm the driver verifies the 5 STRATA- reg rows in the fixture and rebuilds + re-grants when they are missing. With that fix the full run at 07:32Z returned NC1-NC5 DISCRIMINATING in ONE uncontended invocation, which closes AC-9 as written.

The seven tool files were unfrozen (chattr -i) to deploy the ensure_fx fix, then re-frozen and re-hashed (p11_frozen_20261020T0739Z.sha256). Until that point the frozen set could not reproduce AC-9 because the defect was inside the frozen bytes.
